subject: Post-demo: model-eval recap + next steps (open-model parity & acceptance)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Matt Hayes <matt.hayes@datahealth.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: model-eval recap + next steps (open-model parity & acceptance)

Hi Matt —

Thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned on evaluation and decision criteria: 

1) What we reviewed
- Demoed Redwood-hosted workflow for inference, KV caching for prompt-heavy flows, and the eval harness we ran on your sample dataset.
- Ran a short benchmark during the call comparing two open models (OpenLM-Large-Quant and OpenCodeX-3B-int8) against your internal baseline (DH-Base-v3) on the sample prompt set.

2) Initial signals
- OpenLM-Large-Quant: matched DH-Base-v3 on intent/slot extraction (~96% macro-f1 on our small set) but showed variance on long-form summarization (ROUGE-L delta ~3.2 pts).
- OpenCodeX-3B-int8: much cheaper, slightly worse on QA recall but 2x faster p95.

3) Concerns you mentioned
- Parity on safety filters and hallucination for clinical notes.
- Need clear acceptance thresholds for recall/precision and latency.

4) Proposed acceptance criteria (suggested starting point)
- Abstractive summarization: ROUGE-L within 3 pts of DH-Base-v3 on your gold prompts.
- Clinical QA: >= 94% answer-precision (no critical hallucinations on safety-critical slots).
- Latency: p95 <= 250ms for 512-token requests on dedicated capacity (we can tune batching).

5) Next steps I propose
A. We share a 3-run eval bundle (attached): eval_results_v1.csv + prompt_sets_for_bench.zip + an initial model-comparison PDF.
B. You run the same eval on DH-Base-v3 and share the gold labels for the acceptance suite (or allow us to run in your VPC if preferred).
C. Align on an acceptance checklist and cutoff dates — propose a 2-week joint eval window starting 2026-03-16.
D. If an open model meets the acceptance criteria, we prepare an MOP (mutual operational plan) and a pilot pricing term for Dedicated capacity.

Attachments: eval_results_v1.csv (small synthetic run), prompt_sets_for_bench.zip, rdw_model_comparison.pdf
Links: https://redwood.app/benchmarks/datahealth-eval (live benchmark), HubSpot deal DH-2026-031

Would you like us to run a quick calibration pass on a larger sample before the 16th, or is the 16th start date OK?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

From: Matt Hayes <matt.hayes@datahealth.ai>

Cc: DataHealth Evaluation Team <eval-team@datahealth.ai>
Date: 2026-03-09T09:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model-eval recap + next steps (open-model parity & acceptance)

Marissa —

Appreciate the clear recap. A couple of clarifications from our side before we lock dates: 

- Gold labels: we can share a de-identified gold set of ~1,200 examples for the acceptance suite. Timing: earliest we can hand that off is 2026-03-12.
- Safety/hallucination: our internal bar is zero critical hallucinations on the 200 safety-critical items in the suite — we'll share those items and how we mark critical.
- DH-Base-v3 numbers: we'll run your attached eval_bundle by EvalsOps and send our baseline metrics by 2026-03-11.

Two asks: 1) Can Redwood provide a brief note on how the open models were tuned (temperature, context-window tricks, any post-processing filters) so our eval run is comparable? 2) For latency, do you have a p50/p95 breakdown across the run (not just mean)?

If those look good, the 2-week window starting 2026-03-16 sounds fine.

Thanks — looking forward.
Matt
Director, Product 
DataHealth Inc

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Matt Hayes <matt.hayes@datahealth.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-09T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: model-eval recap + next steps (open-model parity & acceptance)

Thanks Matt — quick technical follow-up from our applied ML team to make the evals comparable.

1) Model config we used (summary):
- OpenLM-Large-Quant: temp=0.0, top_p=0.95, max_tokens=1024, KV prefix caching enabled. Quantized to 8-bit integer kernels; no additional instruction-tuning applied.
- OpenCodeX-3B-int8: temp=0.0, top_p=0.9, max_tokens=512; minimal post-processing (simple answer-trimming + heuristic safety filter).

2) Why we saw the ROUGE gap: for longer, multi-paragraph clinical summaries the open model sometimes compresses content differently (more extractive) which reduces ROUGE-L even when semantic content is fine. We recommend including an entailment-based check (NLI) as a secondary quality metric for the final acceptance to avoid over-reliance on n-gram scores.

3) Latency breakdown (from the attached run):
- OpenLM-Large-Quant: p50=82ms, p95=210ms (512 tokens, dedicated GPU pool with batching disabled for calibration);
- OpenCodeX-3B-int8: p50=48ms, p95=110ms.

4) Suggested acceptance thresholds (refined):
- Summarization: ROUGE-L delta <= 3 pts OR entailment >= 0.92 on the acceptance set.
- Clinical QA: precision >= 94% AND no >0 critical hallucinations across the 200 safety items.
- Latency: p95 <= 250ms for the production config (we can tune batching and autoscale).

5) Operational ask: if parity is achieved on the acceptance set, we'll recommend a pilot on Redwood Dedicated with a canary route and an automatic fallback to DH-Base-v3 for any requests that fail safety checks. We can include a monitoring hook that triggers rollback on quality regressions greater than 2 pts ROUGE on a rolling 24h window.

I'll drop a short tech note in the Drive folder with the exact command-lines we used for the attached eval. Let us know if you'd rather we run within your VPC for the gold set — both are possible.

-Neha
Senior Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: eval_results_v1.csv (CSV, 1.2MB)]

Neha / Marissa —

This is great, thanks for the details. Two quick confirmations: 
1) We'll hand off the de-identified gold set on 2026-03-12.
2) We'll run your attached eval_bundle on DH-Base-v3 and return baseline metrics by 2026-03-11.

We prefer Redwood to run inside our VPC for the gold set (data transfer & audit trail reasons). Please send a short runbook/required IAM roles and we'll provision access by 2026-03-13.

Also, please include the automatic fallback + rollback policy language in the MOP draft. If open model meets acceptance criteria in the 2-week window we are prepared to move to a 6-week paid pilot on Dedicated capacity for a single business unit.

I'll loop in procurement during the pilot discussion but for now this is a green light to proceed with the eval cadence.

Matt
